subject: Privacy-first hosting recap & required asks (HelioMed discovery)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Jay Singh <jay.singh@heliomed.com>, Ravi Patel <r.patel@heliomed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Privacy-first hosting recap & required asks (HelioMed discovery)

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap from our side and the concrete asks to keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard (pain / goals):
- Primary requirement: PHI must remain within US-controlled infrastructure and be logically segregated per tenant.
- Regulatory driver: state-level payer audits + upcoming HIPAA readiness review in Q1.
- Technical constraints: customer network is restrictive (no egress to public IPs except approved endpoints), onboarding team prefers an offline upgrade path (air-gap considerations).
- Non-functional: low-latency inference for batch adjudication (~100ms p50 target), and a predictable cost band for pilot.

Open questions we flagged (please confirm):
1) Can you confirm the NetOps contact and the team that owns the firewall rules? We need an ingress/egress matrix and preferred IP ranges.
2) Is HSM (FIPS 140-2) integration required for key management or will KMS be sufficient?
3) Will there be a maintenance window cadence constraint for on-prem components?

Immediate next steps (ask list):
- Jay / Ravi: share a basic network diagram (VLANs, NAT/Gateway, firewall vendor) and any corporate IP allowlist policies — target: by Oct 4.
- Redwood (Camila): share our Private Hosting checklist and a sample SOW for an isolated deployment (attached).
- Technical deep-dive: schedule a 60m host/network session with NetOps + Redwood infra engineers (proposed week of Oct 11).
- Security: if helpful, we can run an on-site or virtual architecture review in week of Oct 18.

Attachments included: redwood-private-checklist.pdf (hosting readiness checklist), sample-sow-template.docx. Also attached a simple network template (heliomed-network-template.xlsx) you can populate.

I'll follow up with available slots for the deep-dive. Thanks — appreciate the clarity on the regulatory drivers, that helps shape our proposed isolation options.

--
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
(Attachment: redwood-private-checklist.pdf; sample-sow-template.docx; heliomed-network-template.xlsx)

From: Jay Singh <jay.singh@heliomed.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Patel <r.patel@heliomed.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privacy-first hosting recap & required asks (HelioMed discovery)

Camila — thanks for the concise write-up, that matches our internal notes. A couple quick clarifications: 

- HSM: yes, we need to see how Redwood would integrate with an HSM for keys used to encrypt PHI at rest. KMS is acceptable only if backed by HSM.
- Offline upgrades: we need a documented upgrade procedure that can run without outbound internet (we have planned maintenance windows with air-gapped segments).
- Timeline: can you give a ballpark for pilot readiness once we sign SOW (rough estimate: 6-10 weeks?) and a cost band for a 6-month pilot with dedicated support?

I'll push to have a network diagram over by Monday (Oct 4). Our NetOps lead is Priya Shah (priya.shah@heliomed.com) — she should be on the deep-dive call.

Thanks — Jay
Jay Singh
Head of Platform Engineering, HelioMed
jay.singh@heliomed.com

Subject: Re: Privacy-first hosting recap & required asks (HelioMed discovery)

Appreciate the quick reply, Jay — answers inline and a proposed plan: 

- HSM / KMS: Redwood supports integration with customer-managed HSMs via our KMS bridge (we can work with PKCS#11-compatible devices). For discovery, we will collect HSM vendor + model and we can validate the integration during the infra deep-dive.

- Offline upgrades / maintenance: we have a documented offline upgrade path for Private deployments. We'll share the playbook as part of the hosting checklist; it includes steps for package staging via approved jump hosts and a validated rollback plan.

- Timeline & cost band: ballpark for pilot (onboarding, network validation, pilot SLA): 8 weeks from SOW signature assuming NetOps provides the network diagram + firewall allowlist within 5 business days. Estimated cost band for a 6-month pilot with reserved capacity & 24x7 support: $90k–$140k (depends on GPU mix and retention settings). We'll firm this up in the SOW.

Next ask from our side: please loop Priya Shah (NetOps) on the network diagram and include any vendor docs for your HSM. Once we have that, we'll schedule the deep-dive (week of Oct 11) and include an infra engineer + security lead.

Shared resources: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3C4HelioMed-Discovery (checklist, SOW template, integration notes).

I'll also attach a short one-pager that explains our HSM integration pattern after the call.

Best,
Camila
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
(Attachment: redwood-private-checklist.pdf)
